top_diagnoses.reasoning_summary: The patient presents with bilateral facial weakness, difficulty closing her eyes, and inability to smile, which are consistent with facial palsy. The nerve conduction study results and absence of limb weakness or sensory loss also support this diagnosis.

Although the patient has elevated CSF protein and partial denervation of facial nerves, the lack of rapidly progressive muscle weakness, areflexia, and nerve conduction velocity slowing makes this diagnosis less likely.
